title: A Physics-Based Digital Twin for Trail Running Race Performance Prediction: A Proof-of-Concept Study
population: 13 trail-running race sessions; Minetti-based grade-adjusted pace model with individual calibration
findings: A grade-adjusted pace model built on Minetti's fifth-degree cost polynomial, with an altitude correction, a TRIMP-based fatigue term and a pacing-decay factor, was calibrated per runner by grid search against 13 race sessions.
Across four stages of model complexity, R2 rose from 0.763 to 0.905.
Leave-one-out cross-validation (n = 13) gave R2 = 0.864, MAE = 18.2 min, MAPE = 11.1% and a small positive bias (+2.0 min).
limitations: Proof of concept on 13 race sessions; the abstract does not say how many runners they came from, and the individual calibration fitted race-level parameters (a sustainable fraction and a pacing-decay slope), not a personal cost-by-grade curve. The model predicts finish time, not speed by grade band.
implications: The Minetti polynomial is in use as the terrain core of an individually calibrated trail model, and leave-one-out validation is the evaluation the authors chose for small personal data; this is the precedent for the leave-one-run-out test in rule I13.
It does not show that a personal cost-by-grade curve beats Minetti; no study found in the corpus search does.

verification.notes: Crossref: Sensors 26(12):3731, 2026-06-11, two authors match. Europe PMC record (PMID 42356703) abstract supports all findings. The number of runners behind the 13 sessions is not in the abstract.
